description:
FILED s513 (Fable, 2026-10-08) from the s513a merge-review probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p2860/s.pl, t.pl; perl 5.40.3 -> main 8d8d37b9 -> the s513a tree 075dd9ed).

perl aliases @_ to the caller's scalar whenever the argument EXPRESSION yields an lvalue, prototype or not:
    sub f ($) { $_[0] .= "!" }   sub g { $_[0] .= "!" }
    my ($c, $u1, $u2) = (1, "u1", "u2");
    f($c ? $u1 : $u2);  print $u1;      # perl u1!   s513a tree u1  (main u1)      <- prototype-only residue
    g($c ? $u1 : $u2);  print $u1;      # perl u1!   main u1!  (the unprototyped path passes the chosen box)
    my $t = "t";
    f(scalar($t));      print $t;       # perl t!    main t, tree t
    g(scalar($t));      print $t;       # perl t!    main t   <- copies on BOTH paths, pre-existing

Two causes:
1. The `$`-slot wrap in Pl/ExprToCL.pm (gen_funcall_form, `$already_scalar`) is a WHITELIST of spellings that are "already a scalar" (Number, Quote, `$` Symbol, `$` Magic, and since s513a an element argbox and a scalar assignment).  A ternary of scalar lvalues, `||` / `//` of lvalues, a parenthesised lvalue, `local $x`, ... are not on it, so they get `(p-scalar ...)` = a COPY, while the unprototyped call passes the expression's box.  The right shape is NOT a longer whitelist: a `$` slot imposes scalar CONTEXT on the argument expression (ir-spec section 5.2, s513a), and the node already receives SCALAR_CTX (`set_node_context`), so the wrap is needed only for an expression that is NOT scalar-valued under that context (an array / hash symbol, a slice, a list, a call whose scalar-context value is the count...) -- invert the test: wrap the aggregate/list shapes, pass everything else exactly as the unprototyped call does.  Measure with corpus-diff: the whitelist today removes 107 wrappers over the corpus (s513a's classify2.out); the inverted rule must remove the same ones and no silent-wrong ones.
2. `scalar(EXPR)` as an argument lowers to a VALUE on both paths (`p-scalar` of the box?); perl's scalar() of an lvalue is still the lvalue.  Smaller; probably the same `p-scalar` reading the box once.

Not a regression: main copies under both spellings.  Bar: s.pl + t.pl == perl; guard rows in Pl/t/proto-alias-01.t (the ternary row inverse-fails on 075dd9ed) and Pl/t/writes-args-01.t (scalar()); corpus-diff explained; the sweep (proto.t, args.t).
subject: SILENT WRONG (residue of #2860, s513a): an argument EXPRESSION that yields a scalar lvalue still copies in two spellings -- `f($c ? $u1 : $u2)` under a `$` prototype (the imposed-scalar p-scalar wrap is a WHITELIST of spellings) and `f(scalar($t))` under any sub
